notes: Prompts for fine-tuning a Piper voice. Read one per recording.
These are ORIGINAL sentences written for this purpose, not corpus extracts.
That is deliberate: it lets the phonetic coverage be controlled, and avoids
tying the training set to any particular text.
Three things they are built to do:
1. Cover the English phoneme inventory and its awkward junctions.
2. Carry the corpus's transliterated names, distributed rather than
clustered, so the model hears them in varied positions.
3. Sit in the register BD actually wants — contemplative and unhurried.
The fine-tune learns DELIVERY, not just timbre: read briskly and the
whole corpus is read briskly for ever.
Each is one utterance, roughly 3-10 seconds. Read at the pace you want the
